whatItDoes: Merges multiple PDF files into a single document with drag-and-drop reordering. Supports up to 20 PDFs, shows page count per file, and preserves all pages and vector content via client-side pdf-lib processing.
whyItExists: Combining PDFs usually requires uploading to a server or installing desktop software. This tool merges PDFs entirely in your browser — no upload, no signup — with explicit page-count feedback and reorder controls so you get the exact document order you need.
whoShouldUse: Students combining assignments, office workers merging reports or invoices, and anyone needing to assemble a single PDF from multiple sources without trusting a third-party server.
useCases: Merge 5 scanned chapter PDFs into one book for reading
Combine 3 invoice PDFs into a single file for accounting
Reorder 2 PDFs by dragging before merging into final submission
Check page counts before merging to verify completeness
Merge PDFs on a slow connection without uploading 50MB to a server
instructions: Click or drop 2–20 PDF files (10MB each, 50MB total). Each shows its page count.
Drag items or use the up/down arrows to set the desired order.
Click Merge — the tool concatenates pages in displayed order using pdf-lib.
Review the green success card showing total pages and file size.
Click Download Merged PDF to save the result. Process is 100% local.
examples: Input: 3 PDFs (2 pages, 1 page, 4 pages) in order B, A, C → Output: 7-page merged PDF in B-A-C order with size sum + overhead.
Input: 2 PDFs each 1 page, reordered via drag → Output: 2-page PDF reflecting the dragged order.
bestPractices: Verify page counts after upload before merging — mismatched counts signal a corrupted file
Keep total under 50MB to avoid browser memory pressure
For large PDFs, merge in batches of 10 if the tab becomes slow
commonMistakes: Dropping non-PDF files — the tool validates MIME and magic bytes and will reject them
Trying to merge encrypted/password-protected PDFs — pdf-lib will report an error
Expecting bookmarks to merge — this version concatenates pages; outline merging is not preserved
faq: Is my PDF uploaded to a server? No — merging happens in your browser via pdf-lib. Files never leave your device.
How many PDFs can I merge? Up to 20 files, 10MB each, 50MB total. Limits follow the 10MB upload rule in File Upload Rules.
Does it preserve quality? Yes — pages are copied vector-for-vector, not rasterized.
Why does dragging matter? Page order in the list is merge order. Drag or use arrows to control it.
features: Page count per file and total size preview
